note: THE MEMBER CHAT: a floating composer, the wrong attach menu, and no admin gate. The founder, on a phone: 'in a chat I can scroll up and down and the input bar moved as well. In a chat hide the bottom menu and put the input text field fixed at the bottom'; 'as an admin if I press on paperclip it appears attach a form, not all that is in community and the same style that we applied'; 'The user, non admin should not have the paperclip.' THE-348 owns the two files below and this is the state it leaves them in. It records NO firestore.rules digest: the rules were read closely and deliberately NOT changed - dmMessages/channelMessages create carry no field allowlist, so the admin gate shipped here is a UI gate and says so in both the component and its guard suite. firestore.indexes.json, functions/ and src/app/layout.tsx are untouched and asserted as such; no npm dependency, no theme token and no new primitive was installed - the attach surface is the AttachMenu THE-331 already built for AdminCommunity, imported rather than copied.

entries.why: THE-348 OWNS this file and this is the state it leaves it in. Four changes: the composer is pinned to the viewport below lg (max-lg:fixed) so it stops travelling with the page, and reserves the home-indicator inset itself now that the nav is hidden; the forms-only 'Attach a Form' sheet is deleted in favour of the shared attach/AttachMenu, which is where the four categories, the recents and the deep-search cascader already live; the paperclip is gated on the CURRENT user's role, derived once off the users doc this file already reads and passed down rather than re-derived a third time; and the five emoji that stood in for icons are gone, replaced by the exported AttachTypeIcon so the chip and the menu cannot drift. The send button gained the 44px phone floor it was missing - it measured 36x36 at 380px. Every one of those is measured in THE-348.member-composer.layout.test.tsx, in a real Chromium. The composer's layer is max-lg:z-10 and NOT the z-[101] it first shipped as: a hit test over the open attach menu's whole box found 22 of 121 sampled pixels covered by the composer, because the menu opens upward from the paperclip and its bottom edge lands in the composer's band while ui/dropdown-menu.tsx paints that menu at its positioner's hardcoded z-50. Inside a conversation the nav is hidden, so there was never anything at 100 for the composer to clear.

THE-348 hides the MEMBER bottom nav while a conversation is open, which is the founder's 'in a chat hide the bottom menu'. The change is deliberately the smallest one this shell admits: the nav already carried a nav-hiding condition for the map tab, so a term was added to it and NO element was introduced - MainApp's element-tree pin is untouched and still passes. The content wrapper stops reserving the nav's 65px band while the nav is hidden, so the fixed composer and the shell do not double-count it. The raising and lowering of the flag live in UserMessages, in an effect with a cleanup, so the nav returns on the back arrow, on switching conversations, on the tab changing and on unmount - #490's lesson that a nav which stays hidden is a trap with no way out. AdminDashboard's own data-nav-shell string is NOT touched: four measured suites discover it by pattern.

THE-348 owns this APPEND and nothing else in the file, exactly as THE-346 owned the one before it and THE-345 the one before that. RULES_PINNERS_NOW goes 64 -> 65 and this ticket's guard suite joins RULES_PINNERS_ADDED_SINCE beside THE-346's entry, never over it - the documented cost of adding a suite that pins firestore.rules through the shared register. No accepted value is widened, no pinner is retired and the exact floor still may not shrink. THE-348 records NO firestore.rules digest anywhere, and that is the whole posture of the ticket rather than an omission: it FOUND a gap - dmMessages and channelMessages create carry no field allowlist, so the rules permit a member to attach by a route that is not the button the founder asked to hide - and it reports that gap as a set of assertions instead of closing it in a file that auto-deploys on merge with no emulator tests. THE-313's one-line change turned 46 files red; a field allowlist on the two hottest write paths in the product is a larger change than that and belongs in a PR that can run the emulator.
